page: Microsoft Azure E48_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Ev5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 252.4 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 126.65 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Passmark memory score and CPU encryption tests also rank in the top 25%. Processing workloads like image processing and static web serving throughput demonstrate strong performance. Conversely, CPU-bound tasks such as stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench compiling, and Redis SET operations perform in the average range. Large-scale LLM inference, specifically text generation for a 70B model, is a notable bottleneck, registering in the bottom 10% at 2.4 tokens per second.

Given the high memory density and lack of local storage, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that rely on external storage systems. The resource profile is highly suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise application servers, and data processing pipelines that require substantial RAM without requiring local NVMe disks or GPU acceleration.

The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators.
